summary:
Sembo – Astraea Mission is an educational interactive game developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, in response to Challenge 3: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The game places children aged 7 to 12 in the role of Commander of a lunar research base, where they must manage a 10-day mission, make important decisions, complete challenges, and ensure the safety of their crew. Through interactive missions, minigames, and decision-making mechanics, players learn about space exploration and the challenges of living and working on the Moon.

Sembo addresses the challenge by transforming scientific knowledge and NASA-based information into an accessible, engaging, and playful learning experience. It also encourages critical thinking, logical reasoning, problem-solving, and teamwork.

The project is important because it helps combat scientific misinformation from an early age, makes reliable scientific knowledge more accessible to children, and inspires curiosity about space exploration and STEM fields. Our goal is to show that learning about the universe can be both educational and fun.
details:
Sembo – Astraea Mission is an educational and interactive game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, in response to Challenge 3: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.

The project aims to reduce scientific misinformation and make space science more accessible to children aged 7 to 12 through a fun, interactive, and educational experience. It introduces scientific information based on verified NASA data in a simple and accessible way, encouraging children to learn while playing.

How does it work?

The game places the player in the role of the Commander of a fictional lunar research base. In the storyline, an international crew of four astronauts is sent to the Moon for a 10-day mission, during which they must conduct experiments, investigate lunar environmental conditions, monitor the base's systems, and ensure the crew's safety.

Throughout the 10 days, the Commander must complete two mandatory missions each day, along with a third randomly selected mission from a database. Each mission presents a situation and different possible decisions. After selecting an option, the player must complete a minigame.

The consequences depend on the player's decisions and performance. Successful minigame completion preserves the consequences associated with the chosen decision, while failure adds an extra 20% penalty. Good decisions lead to positive outcomes, whereas poor decisions can compromise the mission and its objectives.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Beyond providing entertainment, Sembo is designed to promote scientific literacy from an early age. By introducing children to real scientific concepts and information from NASA, the game encourages curiosity about space exploration and helps distinguish reliable scientific information from misinformation.

It also promotes the development of important skills, including:

  • Critical thinking: evaluating situations before making decisions.
  • Problem-solving: finding solutions to unexpected challenges.
  • Logical reasoning: understanding the consequences of different choices.
  • Communication: recognizing the importance of teamwork in space missions.
  • Decision-making: taking responsibility for choices and their outcomes.

Our intended impact is to make scientific knowledge more accessible to younger audiences, inspire an interest in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics), and encourage the next generation to explore science and space.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed using accessible digital tools and programming technologies:

  • HTML5: for the structure of the website and game.
  • CSS3: for the visual design, layout, and interface.
  • JavaScript: for the game mechanics, interactions, missions, and decision-making system.
  • Visual Studio Code (VS Code): as the main development environment.
  • Sketchbook: for creating the original illustrations and visual elements.
  • Google Drive: for organizing the storyline and written content.
  • Google Translate: as a language-support tool during content development.
  • Canva: for the project's presentation materials.
  • GitHub Pages: for hosting the game and making it publicly accessible without requiring installation.

Creativity and Innovation

The main creative aspect of Sembo is the combination of scientific education, storytelling, interactive gameplay, and decision-making.

Instead of presenting scientific information through traditional lessons or static texts, the game transforms knowledge about space exploration into practical challenges. Players experience a fictional lunar mission in which their decisions directly influence the development of the story and the safety of the crew.

The project also draws inspiration from NASA's Artemis II mission, incorporating the idea of an international astronaut crew with different areas of expertise. Its fictional lunar research base allows children to explore the challenges of living and working beyond Earth in an engaging and accessible way.

The name Astraea was inspired by Greek mythology. Associated with the stars and the constellation Virgo, Astraea represents the connection between humanity and the universe, reflecting the project's central themes of curiosity, discovery, and exploration.

Factors Considered During Development

Throughout development, our team considered several important factors to ensure the game would be educational, engaging, and appropriate for its target audience.

First, we prioritized accessibility and age-appropriate communication, ensuring that scientific concepts could be understood by children aged 7 to 12 without unnecessary technical complexity.

We also considered scientific accuracy, seeking to base the educational content on reliable and verified NASA information rather than fictional scientific claims.

Another important factor was gameplay engagement. We developed different scenarios, characters, missions, and minigames to maintain players' interest throughout the 10-day experience.

Finally, we considered the educational value of player decisions. By introducing consequences for different choices, the game encourages children to think critically, understand cause and effect, and recognize the importance of responsibility and teamwork.

Our team aimed to create more than just a game: we wanted to develop an educational experience that brings science closer to children and demonstrates that learning about the universe can be both meaningful and enjoyable.
